categories.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
categories.description: Hardcoded keys, env var leaks, and sensitive credential theft from .cursor/mcp.json and similar configs

categories.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
categories.description: Overly broad tool permission definitions allowing agents to gain unnecessary system control or data access

categories.name: Tool Poisoning
categories.description: Legitimate MCP tools tampered with or injected with malicious logic returning falsified results to manipulate the model

categories.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks
categories.description: Dependency tampering, malicious third-party MCP servers, or backdoors in build scripts

categories.name: Command Injection & Execution
categories.description: Agent constructs and executes system commands, shell scripts, or API calls based on untrusted input

categories.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
categories.description: Malicious instructions injected through context (OCR, web content) hijacking model control flow

categories.name: Insufficient Auth & Authorization
categories.description: MCP servers or tools failing to verify identity, leading to cross-agent or cross-user privilege escalation

categories.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
categories.description: Missing tamper-proof logging of tool calls and context changes, hindering security forensics

categories.name: Shadow MCP Servers
categories.description: Unauthorized MCP instances deployed with default configurations, lacking security compliance

categories.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
categories.description: Sensitive context shared across sessions or agents, leading to information disclosure or logic interference

categories.name: Name Confusion Attack
categories.description: Malicious tools registered with names similar to legitimate tools to trick agents into calling the wrong one

categories.name: Rug Pull Attack
categories.description: Malicious MCP service that suddenly terminates or changes behavior after gaining trust, causing DoS or data loss

categories.name: Tool Shadowing Attack
categories.description: Overriding legitimate tool behavior by redefining tools with the same name

categories.name: CORS Misconfiguration
categories.description: Misconfigured Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policies that could allow unauthorized cross-domain access to MCP servers
